paragraphs: Salford City Council runs its own not-for-profit fostering service and is part of Foster for Greater Manchester, a partnership of all ten Greater Manchester councils that aims to keep children at the same school and close to where they come from. Children from Salford may also live with independent agencies such as those listed on this page.

The council pays each child's weekly boarding allowance plus a skills payment that rises as carers complete free training. Every carer starts at level 2. The boarding allowance runs from £169 a week for a baby to £256 for a 16 or 17-year-old, and the skills payment is £106, £160 or £220 a week at levels 2, 3 and 4, so a carer at level 2 looking after a child aged 5 to 10 receives £298 a week. There are yearly birthday and festival, holiday and prom allowances on top. Its Focus scheme gives more intensive support and a financial package designed to let one carer stay at home full time.

New carers complete Skills to Foster before approval, then a rolling programme of day and evening training and a first-year workbook leading to an accredited award. Each household has a family placement social worker, a buddy carer, a 24/7 emergency phone line and access to support groups, including a group for carers' own children. The council can also provide equipment such as beds, car seats and stair gates.
Before deciding, compare what the council offers with two or three of the agencies below, and ask each about pay, training and support near you.
